source.title: Model Theory of Tame Valued Fields and Beyond: Recent Developments and Open Questions

accepted.question_text: Let (K,v) be a tame valued field, meaning a henselian valued field whose algebraic closure with the unique extension of v is a tame extension. Do tame valued fields admit quantifier elimination in some suitable expansion of the language of valued rings? The surrounding discussion indicates that the obstruction is poor understanding of purely wild extensions, i.e. algebraic extensions of a henselian valued field that are linearly disjoint from tame extensions.

evidence.quote:
Open problem 1: Do tame fields admit quantifier elimination in a suitable lan
guage?

The problem is that we do not know enough about purely wild extensions, i.e.,
algebraic extensions of a henselian valued field that are linearly disjoint from tame
extensions.

accepted.question_text: Consider the maximal immediate extensions of the valued fields Q_p(ζ_{p^∞}) and Q_p(p^{1/p^∞}) produced in Kartas's work, where some of these maximal immediate extensions have decidable elementary theories and uncountably many have distinct elementary theories. What is the structure of these maximal immediate extensions, beyond the fact that they are infinite, and which structural features distinguish the decidable extensions from the undecidable ones?

evidence.quote:
Kartas shows that there are uncountably many maximal immediate extensions
with distinct elementary Lval-theories. This implies that uncountably many of them
are not decidable.

Open problem 2: What is the structure of these extensions (apart from the fact
that they are infinite)? What are the indications in their structure that distinguish
the decidable from the undecidable extensions?

accepted.question_text: Are the valued fields Q_p(ζ_{p^∞}), Q_p(p^{1/p^∞}), and Q_p^{ab} decidable in the language Lval of valued rings? Are the positive-characteristic analogues F_p((t))^{1/p^∞} and F_p^{ac}((t))^{1/p^∞} decidable in Lval, or even in the richer language Lval(t) with a constant symbol for t?
accepted.context_brief: Decidability of infinite local and perfect-hull extensions

accepted.question_text: Kartas proves implications from decidability of the positive-characteristic perfectoid-side fields to decidability of the mixed-characteristic fields Q_p(ζ_{p^∞}), Q_p(p^{1/p^∞}), and Q_p^{ab}. Can one prove a reverse transfer principle in the non-complete setting that goes back from mixed characteristic to positive characteristic, and more precisely can one strengthen the known argument so as to recover decidability in the language Lval(t) on the positive-characteristic side?

evidence.quote: Open problem 4: What about the reverse direction?

So a more precise version
of problem 4 is whether this argument can be improved to get decidability in Lval(t)
on the positive characteristic side.

accepted.question_text: What model-theoretic statements can be proved for (roughly) deeply ramified valued fields relative to their value groups and residue fields? In particular, what can be said about the model theory of the perfect hull F_p((t))^{1/p^∞}, which is discussed as a central example of a deeply ramified field that remains outside the existing tame and roughly tame transfer results?

This question is motivated by the positive result that F_p(t^{1/p^∞})^h is an elementary substructure of F_p((t))^{1/p^∞}.

accepted.question_text: In the setting of Kuhlmann's incomplete axiom systems for F_p((t)), one can construct henselian defectless extensions that satisfy the basic axioms but fail existential closedness in maximal immediate extensions because of behavior of additive polynomials. Is there a simple and usable extra condition on the immediate extensions that repairs this failure and yields a satisfactory axiomatization?

accepted.question_text: Let (A) denote the elementary axiom system "henselian defectless valued field of positive characteristic with value group a Z-group and residue field F_p." If one adds the axiom scheme asserting that the valued field is extremal, does the resulting theory become complete?

evidence.quote:
Theorem 13 (Kuhlmann (2001)). The Lval-elementary axiom system
(A) "henselian defectless valued field of positive characteristic with value group a
Z-group and residue field Fp"
is not complete.
Open problem 10: Is (A) + "(K, v) is extremal" a complete axiom system?

accepted.question_text: Suppose a valuation v decomposes as v = w ◦ ̄w, where both w and ̄w are extremal and the value group of w is divisible. Must the composite valuation v also be extremal?

evidence.quote:
we do not entirely know how extremality behaves

group, does it follow that v is extremal?

accepted.question_text: Suppose a valuation v factors as v = w ◦ ̄w and v itself is extremal. It is known that the induced valuation ̄w must then be extremal. Does extremality of v also force the coarser factor w to be extremal?
accepted.context_brief: Descent of extremality to a coarsening

accepted.question_text: Is every extremal valued field existentially closed in its maximal immediate extensions? This is asked after observing that a particular extension (L,v) of F_p((t)) fails this existential-closedness property and, by a theorem cited in the paper, is therefore not extremal.

evidence.quote:
Finally, let us mention that in the extension (L, v) of Fp((t)) constructed in [28]
not all images of additive polynomials have the optimal approximation property ...
This gives rise to the following

imal immediate extensions?

accepted.question_text: Does hypothesis (R4) hold? Here (R4) is the assertion that for an arbitrary field K, if F|K is an extension admitting a K-rational place, then K is existentially closed in F. The paper explains that local uniformization would imply (R4), and that (R4) would in turn yield decidability of the existential Lval(t)-theory of F_p((t)).

evidence.quote:
In the paper [2] the assumption that implication 1)⇒3) holds for arbitrary fields
K is called hypothesis (R4). Hence local uniformization implies (R4).
Open problem 14: Does (R4) hold?

accepted.question_text: Does local uniformization by alteration imply a useful analogue of (R4), namely an "(R4) by alteration" statement, and more generally is there a satisfactory form of "model theory by alteration" in which one is allowed to pass to finite extensions in order to recover the desired existential-closedness or decidability conclusions?

evidence.quote:
In the paper [16] de Jong proved resolution by alteration, which means that a
finite extension of the function field of the algebraic variety under consideration is
taken into the bargain.

Open problem 15: Does local uniformization by alteration imply a reasonable
(and useful) hypothesis "(R4) by alteration"? Is there a "model theory by alter
ation"?

accepted.question_text: Let (K,v) be a henselian valued field. Assume that every algebraic extension of (K,v) is an independent defect field in the sense defined in the paper via Galois extensions of prime degree with nontrivial defect. Does it follow that (K,v) must already be a roughly deeply ramified field?

evidence.quote:
In view of Theorem 9, we conjecture that a henselian field is a roughly deeply
ramified field if and only if all of its algebraic extensions are independent defect
fields. Thus we ask:

Open problem 16: If all algebraic extensions of a henselian field (K, v) are
independent defect fields, does it follow that (K, v) is a roughly deeply ramified
field?
